No episode clearly or genuinely uncertainly met the requested unsupported-slogan or explicit-protection criteria: recurrent assertions about knowledge, probability, and moderation accompany substantive arguments and later qualifications.

contrasts.speaker: A
contrasts.quote: there are still hundreds of texts that are in dispute
contrasts.explanation: Wallace expressly limits his reassuring percentage claim: meaningful variants remain, and hundreds of passages depend on the reading selected. His preceding examples at E1513–1567 illustrate consequential differences. This qualification prevents the percentage from functioning as a blanket dismissal of textual uncertainty.

contrasts.speaker: B
contrasts.quote: I think historians have to weigh probabilities
contrasts.explanation: Ehrman distinguishes uncertainty about exact wording from wholesale textual unreliability, judging a completely different original Mark improbable. This qualifies his repeated claims that 'we don't know'; E2615–2626 also identifies hypothetical manuscript evidence he would accept as good evidence.
